Commentary.Commentary: England, on the other hand, will look for a wicket or two, especially that of Kuhn. Stay tuned...
The Proteas will have around 15-20 minutes to bat till Lunch. Their sole aim will be to see off this period without any wickets lost.

South Africa bowled pretty well for most part of the innings but the counter-attack from Bairstow ruffled them. Morne Morkel was probably the unluckiest bowler with only 2 wickets while Rabada was the best with 4 scalps. Olivier and Maharaj picked up 2 apiece.

A decent batting effort from England, looking at the final score. As mentioned yesterday, apart from Bairstow, no one converted the start. Today morning it was all about Jonny Bairstow and how crucial he is to this English side. Might be a good case to try and push him up the order. Wonder how de Kock must be feeling - he dropped Bairstow on 53 with the partnership on 0 then.

England are in a much better position thanks to this 50-run stand between Bairstow and Anderson. They would have come this morning to try and get as close to 400 but they lost their way, with 3 wickets down for 41 runs. But Bairstow then exploded from 53 to reach 99, unluckily missing his century.

OUT! LBW! The decision stays! Bairstow has to depart on 99. It was full and outside off, Bairstow got down with a huge stride to sweep but missed. Umpire Dharmasena thought for a while and then raised his finger. Bairstow immediately went for the review, given that he had no other choice and the impact was UMPIRE'S CALL. Only just. Tough luck for him. A thin line of difference between 99 and 100. ENGLAND ARE ALL OUT FOR 362!
Bairstow has been adjudged LBW on 99! He reviews it though... Tick, tick, tick... Bairstow's heartbeat...
Full and around middle, Bairstow goes inside out and drives it towards cover.
On middle and leg, defended from the crease.
Full and outside off, pushed to the off side.
On middle and leg, stays low a touch, defended to the leg side. Over to you, Jonny! Massive applause from the crowd.
A short ball down the leg side, Jimmy instinctively goes to tuck it away but misses.
50-run stand is up as well! South Africa losing the plot a bit here.
Is that a mistake? Bairstow takes the single with two balls to spare. Short and wide outside off, Jonny cuts it to the man in the deep at point and this time he gets only a single. Moves to 99...
Full and outside off, a touch wide, eased through the covers for another couple. Dean Elgar in the deep takes his own sweet time to release the ball and the brace is completed with ease.

Excellent running! Outside off, Bairstow punches it through the covers, calls for two and runs hard. Anderson puts on his roller skates and in the end, he has to dive to get in. Bairstow applauds the effort.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
Outside off, left alone.
Outside off, a play and a miss as he plays inside the line.
FOUR! Outside off, Anderson gets off the mark with a cut behind point.
Around off and middle, Anderson gets across and defends it towards the leg side. Better from Jimmy.

NOT OUT! But a risky shot with your partner 6 short of a ton. Landed outside off, Anderson shaped to play the reverse sweep but missed with the ball spinning in. He got hit on the pads and Maharaj appealed. It was not given and du Plessis reviewed it, only to find the ball clipping the top of leg stump. Close. Very close. Immediately Bairstow has a word with his partner.
Huge appeal for LBW! Is Anderson gone? He has been adjudged not out and South Africa want it reviewed...
Landed outside off, spinning in a long way, Anderson pushes but misses.
KESHAV MAHARAJ into the attack now. Can he break this partnership?

FOUR! Moves to 94 but Anderson will be on strike in the next over. Back of a length outside off, Bairstow goes back and across and guides it behind point. Third man starts to race across but the ball wins the race. To be honest, he would be happy that the ball won the race.
Outside off, Bairstow walks across and defends.

SIX! Ho ho ho! This is serious batting. Bairstow charges into the 90s with a terrific shot. If the previous ball was a scoop, the batsman understands in advance that the length will be shorter. Jumps down the track and smashes it past Anderson into the Jimmy Anderson end!

FOUR! Improvisation! Bairstow into limited-overs mode! He walks across his stumps, picks this from a length and scoops it over fine leg for a boundary! Olivier smiles. That is all he can do. Unexpected from the batsman.
A length ball outside off, Bairstow flashes hard but does not move his feet and misses.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
DUANNE OLIVIER to bowl now.
Poor bowling, on the pads, that too on the final ball, easy single given away as JB works it behind square leg.
FOUR! Very late cut. Nicely played. He likes that shot. Stays back to this one and dabs it pretty late behind gully to third man.
Outside off, Jonny flashes but misses.
Another useful stroke. Clips it through the leg side and earns a brace.
Outside off, chipped over cover for a couple.
Full and outside off, pushed towards long on. Anderson jogs halfway through, only to be sent back.

ALMOST A RUN OUT! Landed outside off, Jonny pushes it towards gully and sets off for a run. Anderson responds blindly, without even waiting to see whether the ball has gone past gully. Bairstow stops on seeing the ball being stopped but because Anderson is halfway through, he decides to run again. The fielder misses his shy at the striker's end and could have had Jimmy.
FOUR! MURDERED! Full and wide outside off, Bairstow reaches out to this one and lofts it over cover for a boundary!
Outside off, punched through the off side.
Outside off, played straight to point.
FOUR! Outstanding timing. Half volley on the pads, Bairstow flicks it a bit uppishly through mid-wicket and the ball races away!
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
Time for the drinks break! South Africa will be very happy with this start for sure. Only one wicket before we see the South African batsmen in the middle.
Defended off the front foot by Anderson presenting the full face of the bat.
Wide down the leg side, left alone.
Good length ball on middle, played to mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Good shot from Bairstow and England will need more of these. That was full on off and driven straight down the ground for a boundary.
Full outside off, played towards point this time.
Bouncer! Bairstow ducks under the bouncer at the last moment.
This one is also down the leg side and the batsman leaves it alone.
No rain forecast but there are a few clouds around.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
On the pads, nudged behind for a single.
Full on off, driven through the covers this time.
Another inside edge onto the pads towards the left of the bowler.
Good length ball on middle, Bairstow looks to flick but gets an edge onto his pads. The ball goes to covers this time.
Leading edge towards covers this time. Single taken.
Outside off, beaten this time.
Edged and through the slips this time. Bairstow is looking tentative after his half century which is odd. He should be settled by now.
Outside off this time, left alone.

Dropped! A full length ball asking for the drive but Bairstow gets an outside edge. De Kock dives for it but fails to keep it in his gloves. The keeper is capable of taking such catches and will not be too pleased.
Full on off. Driven towards the mid off region.
Struck on the pads this time but it was not in front of the stumps.
Beaten outside off. That was asking for a drive but Anderson failed to get any bat to it.
Back of a length, defended solidly by Anderson.
James Anderson is the new man in.

OUT! Bowled 'em! Morne Morkel gets his man! Pitched on a fuller length around off, it swings in. Broad is all over this ball as he misses the straight drive completely. The ball goes on to strike the timber as England lose their ninth wicket!
Streaky! FOUR nevertheless. That was slightly wide outside off and Broad went for the drive which flew over gully for a boundary. Broad won't mind them as long as they keep coming.
Short ball outside off, Bairstow stays on his back foot and cuts it past pint for a single.
Nudged down fine leg this time for a single.

Gets an inside edge this time as it goes on to strike his pads. This was on off and middle and Bairstow is lucky to get some bat on it. Ouch! That must have hurt as the ball went on to strike his box.
Outside off, play and miss from Bairstow.
Full length ball outside off, pushed through the covers for three runs.
Stuart Broad is the new man in.

OUT! Ali has to go! His aggressiveness gets the better of him. It was a length ball just outside off and Ali went a punch off his back foot. The ball took an outside edge and went straight to Faf du Plessis at second slip. Good clean catch from the South African skipper.
Defends this one from within the crease.
Outside off, Bairstow shoulders his arms at it.
17th Test fifty for Bairstow, 3rd of this series. It has been a fighting knock which includes eight boundaries so far.
FOUR! Good looking square cut from Bairstow for a boundary. He is looking in good touch at the moment. Another 50 for the batsman as he fights on for England.
On the pad once again. This time Bairstow works it down the leg side for a couple.
Struck on the pads but it looks safe.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
FOUR!  What a shot from Ali! That was short from Rabada and it got the treatment. Ali rocked back and pulled it past mid-wicket for a boundary.
Pushed towards covers but straight to the fielder. That was slightly full from Rabada.
Shows the full face of the bat to defend this one off the back foot.
Driven through the covers this time. That was full and the shot was well timed. Two runs taken.
FOUR! Short ball on leg this time. Ali looks to pull and it looks like he manages to get something off his bat. The ball goes very fine down the leg side for a boundary.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back oot.
Four Leg byes! On the pads this time. Bairstow looks to flick but misses. The ball goes off his pads towards the boundary rope at fine leg. What an expensive over this! 12 runs from this one.
Shows the full face of the bat to defend this one.
FOUR! Punched off the back foot through the covers this time. The fielder gave a hearty chase but it was all in vain. Two boundaries already in this over.
Shows the full face of the bat to defend this one on middle off his back foot.
FOUR! Edged this one but it goes safely over gully. That was a full length ball outside off and Bairstow drives hard at it, good that he did as well. Welcome runs for England and Bairstow.
Bairstow chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
FOUR! Full on middle. Ali drives it beautifully through mid on for a boundary. Well timed by the all-rounder on this occasion.
Back of a length this time, defended off the back foot by Ali.
Ali misses this one outside off. That was close to the edge of the bat and the new man needs to be careful.
Bouncer! Ali ducks under it.
Moeen Ali is the new man in.

Out! Gone! Smart catch at short point by Bavuma as Rabada gets his man! The nightwatchman has done his part you can say. This was again a full length ball on off. Toby went for the drive but played it straight into the hands of Bavuma. The South African took a good sharp catch there as he had very little time to react. South Africa will be delighted with this start!
FOUR! Good shot from Roland-Jones this time. Back-to-back boundaries from England. This was full on off and Toby drives it beautifully through covers for a boundary.
FOUR! Wristy shot! This was on middle and leg, Bairstow flicks it nicely through the leg side at the square leg region for a boundary.
Another play and miss. Morkel is really on top of Bairstow!
In the corridor of uncertainty. Bairstow looks to play but misses it completely. Morkel is coming very close to getting a wicket.
Shout for lbw not given! That was full angling towards the leg side. Bairstow looked for the flick but misses. The umpire was not interested as the ball was going on to miss the leg stump.
Back of a length on middle and leg, played to mid-wicket this time.
This time he finds the edge but the ball lands safely towards point. That was a good length ball on middle and off as Bairstow looked to play at it.

No ball! Oooh! Hint of away movement as he bowls a good length ball just outside off. Bairstow misses it comepletely. Could have easily been an edge to the keeper. However it would not have mattered as Morkel overstepped.
Bye! Down the leg side but Bairstow goes for it. He misses and the ball goes past the keeper to fine leg. Bye taken.
Once again back of a length around off, played nicely to mid-wicket.
Another one on a good length, played to mid-wicket.
Bouncer this time, ducked well by Bairstow. It was going well down the leg side but de Kock did very well to gather it.
Back of a length on middle and leg. Roland-Jones looks to pull but misses. The ball brushes off his thigh pad and goes towards fine leg. Leg bye has been taken.
Silly point is in place!
Fullish on off, pushed towards covers this time.
Good length ball on off, defended towards the off side towards covers. No runs again, another maiden over.
Fuller length ball on middle. Drives it towards mid on.
On a good length but outside off this time. Left alone.
Similar delivery as the one before this. Bairstow deals with it in the same way as well.
This one is aimed at middle and leg, on a good length. Bairstow displays a good looking front foot defense.
Starts off with a good length ball just outside off. Bairstow tries to punch it off his back foot but misses.
Morne Morkel will be bowling from the other end.
Beaten once again! This one was angling in with the arm. Roland-Jones went for a drive but missed it completely. Maiden over and a good start by Rabada!
Hint of swing there as Toby goes for one outside off. The ball goes just past his outside edge on this occasion.
Back of a length this time, Roland-Jones defends it off his back foot.
On a length on off, played off the front foot and into the ground. Solid defense there.
Bowls this one wide outside off looking for an edge again, Toby leaves it alone.
Starts off with a testing ball on middle and leg. Toby looked to flick but got a leading edge which went to covers. Good start by Rabada!
It's bright and sunny at Old Trafford as the players walk out! Rabada will begin proceedings with ball and the nightwatchman Toby Roland-Jones will take the strike.

From South Africa's perspective, early wickets will be the key. If they can bowl like how they did yesterday, we can expect Dean Elgar and Heino Kuhn to come in to bat soon. Lastly, the rain gods are keeping away and the forecast is good for the start of the day with showers expected later on. Let's hope the wind pushes the dark clouds away if and when they come! Stay tuned for another action-packed day of cricket!

How can they do that? First things first, survive the morning conditions and try not to lose wickets in the first session. We have seen that the batting conditions were getting better as the day progressed so they can get to that elusive score of 400.

Welcome back to Old Trafford for the second day of the fourth Test between England and South Africa. The hosts have not had the kind of start they would have expected. Nevertheless it is an all new day and a fresh good start can take them to a respectable position.
...Day 2, Session 1...

What is the verdict? Whom does Day 1 belong to? It has been an even one but guess because of the batting line-up that England possess and also because South Africa are without Vernon Philander, taking 6 wickets gives them a 60 percent share. They will look to restrict England under 300 who themselves will aim to get as close to 400 as possible. Join us at 1100 local (1000 GMT) to find out how Day 2 pans out. In the meanwhile, you can also check out how the second Sri Lanka-India Test is going about. Adios! Take Care!

England will be a bit disappointed at the way they batted today. Four batsmen got starts but failed to convert them into big ones. Especially that wicket of Ben Stokes will hurt them the most as he could have been very destructive on Saturday with the bat. They still have some batting left with Moeen Ali in the wings.

One can be a bit critical and say the Proteas DID NOT make full use of the conditions in the morning. If they had bowled better, they could have got more than a solitary wicket. They managed to keep the runs in check though and kept pegging away. Towards the end of the day, with the second new ball, they leaked a few runs but managed to get the dangerous Ben Stokes in the penultimate over. Morne Morkel picked up just one wicket but the figures don't show how well he bowled. He constantly kept asking questions and got the ball to move around. Rabada was the best bowler, with 2 wickets while Olivier got a couple as well but one must say he was very inconsistent. Maharaj kept it tight at one end and got the big wicket of Cook.

South Africa walk off the field, feeling pretty satisfied with themselves. They have bowled their heart out, taking 6 wickets on the opening day. Also, they have not allowed a terrific batting line-up like England's to score quickly which gives them full marks.
Landed outside off, Bairstow does not flirt with that. STUMPS ON DAY 1!
Outside off, left alone.
FOUR! A bit streaky now. On a good length outside off, Bairstow looks to defend but then decides to withdraw his bat. Is late and the ball goes off the outside edge behind gully to third man.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! MAGNIFICENT! Half volley outside off, Bairstow leans and drives it through extra cover for a boundary!
Landed outside off, coming in a long way, Bairstow looks to tuck it away but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
TOBY ROLAND-JONES walks in ahead of Moeen Ali at number 8, replacing Stokes.

OUT! Perfect yorker! Rabada roars. Old Trafford is plunged into silence. What a ball at what an hour. He gives it his best on his very last ball of the day. Delivers a terrific yorker, around middle and off, watches Stokes' bat come down late and then sees and hears timbaaaa!!!! Beautiful ball. Excellent innings from Stokes but England would have wished to see him tomorrow with the willow.
FOUR! A bit streaky in my opinion. On a length outside off, seaming away, Stokes looks to run it down to third man but the ball runs off the outer half of the bat, behind point to the fence.
The batsman gets an inside edge and the ball hits him on the pads.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off.

EDGED, FOUR! A good testing ball, that too, at this time of the day. Rabada bangs it in short and Stokes is beaten by pace. He is late into the pull shot and is cramped for room. Halfway through the shot, he looks to abort it but is late and gets a top edge which goes over de Kock to the fine leg fence.
Landed around middle and off, watchfully defended.
Outside off, pretty wide, left alone.
Landed outside off, defended from the crease.
UPPISH, BUT SAFE! Full and outside off, swinging away, Jonny plays at the ball away from his body and does so uppishly, but luckily for him, it goes in the gap behind point. Two runs taken.
Landed outside off, a tad fuller, left alone.
That comes in a long way from outside off, Bairstow misses his tuck and is hit high on the pads, above the knee roll.
Landed outside off, let through.
DUANNE OLIVIER back into the attack from the newly named Jimmy Anderson end. Can he replicate what Jimmy usually does at the fag end of the day?
Played to the mid-wicket region by the batsman. One run added to the total.
Full and outside off, driven straight to cover.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Another lovely ball, this time keeping it back of a length, outside off, a tentative Jonny feels for it and misses.
Short and outside off, cut straight to cover-point.
Landed outside off, Bairstow pushes inside the line but finds the ball jagging off the seam away from him, to beat the outside edge.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Full and outside off, Bairstow leans and drives it beautifully through the covers. Does not have enough on it to make the ball reach the ropes. Three runs taken.
Outside off, played straight to point.
50-run stand comes up as well. Runs coming thick and fast with this second new ball.

FOUR BYES! That went away a long way. It was pitched on a length, outside off, Bairstow felt for it and nearly nicked it. However, the ball moved away a long way and found its way through the slip cordon to the third man fence.
Around middle and off, pushed straight to mid on.
Full on middle, clipped straight to short mid-wicket.
10th Test Fifty for Ben Stokes! What a player. Century in the last game, half century so far.
A length ball outside off, driven wide of mid off for a couple. Another quality innings from the southpaw.
That is a beauty! On a length across the batsman, shapes away, Stokes pushes at it but fails to make any contact. The ball whizzes past the outside edge.
Angles this across the left-hander, Ben lets it go past.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman.
Fullish on middle and leg, clipped straight to short mid-wicket.
Outside off, left alone.
On middle and leg, flicked through the leg side for a couple.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Outside off, left alone.
Landed outside leg, Stokes looks to flick and the ball goes off the pads to square leg. A leg bye is taken but no signal comes from the umpire. Must have been an inside edge then.
The batsman has attempted to put bat on ball - but fails.
Outside off, left alone.
On the pads, flicked through mid-wicket. Maharaj and de Bruyn chase it in pairs with the former getting to the ball and sliding to save the boundary. Three runs taken.

OUCH! That would have hurt! Back of a length on leg stump, Stokes swivels to pull but is beaten as the ball stays a touch low. He gets an inside edge and is hit on the thigh. Is down in pain but Stokesy is a brave lad.
Outside off, a play and a miss.
Outside off, Bairstow punches it through point where Temba Bavuma makes a good stop to keep the batsmen to a single.
Played to the point region by the batsman.
Landed outside off, on a length, then moves away off the pitch, Bairstow feels for it but misses.
KAGISO RABADA to share the second new ball with the Giraffe.
The batsman goes after a wide one and misses.

EDGED! FOUR! Well, you have taken the new ball for a reason. Wickets. Why not keep an attacking field? Morne keeps it on a length outside off and induces the drive and later, the outside edge. The ball flies to the slip cordon but to an unmanned third slip and then to the third man fence! Surprised to see Faf not attacking, especially with only a few overs to the close.
Landed outside off, angling away, Ben takes his bat out of the way this time but is late again, getting beaten once more.
Full and outside off, Stokes feels for it and just about nicks it! Luckily for him, the ball shapes away to beat the outside edge.
Outside off, comes in a long way, Bairstow gets his bat down at the last moment and works it through mid-wicket for a single.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
MORNE MORKEL to make the first use of the new cherry.
THE SECOND NEW BALL has been taken. Wonder why this 1-over delay. Perhaps Faf wanted Morne to make the first use of the second new ball and the latter wanted this particular end.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

Ha ha ha, sloppy from Bavuma. Ben defends this to the leg side and both Bavuma from silly mid on and Maharaj look to get to the ball. Bavuma gets there first but Maharaj is almost there as well. However, Bavuma does not know that and back-flicks the ball, thinking that Maharaj will take it. But Maharaj is beside him and as a result, the ball goes past the stumps. Maharaj quickly rushes to collect it and then turns out, only to see neither of Bairstow or Stokes even the least bit interested in the overthrow. But he is definitely unhappy with Bavuma.
Fullish on middle, pushed towards the bowler.
Full and wide outside off, Stokes looks to drive but gets it from the inner half of the bat towards silly mid on.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Landed outside off, spinning in nicely, punched towards mid off.
The second new ball is available. The Proteas are deliberating on whether to take it or not. Looks like they will wait it out. Reviews have been refreshed as well.
Length ball outside off, pushed towards covers for a single.

Stokes goes across and looks to flick this one. The shot was on as the ball was on good length towards his pads but he misses it completely. He gets struck on the pads but it was outside the line of the leg stump.
Back of a length, punched off the back foot by Stokes.
Fuller in length, driven towards mid off.
Outside off, pushed towards covers but straight to the fielder.
Gets right behind the line of this good length ball and defends it.
Full length ball on middle, defended off the front foot and into the ground.
Good length ball on middle, played it towards mid-wicket this time.
Outside off, Bairstow looks for the swep but mistimes it. He plays straight behind the keeper and picks up a single. That could have easily been a catch.
Flighted on off, played towards point but straight to the fielder.
Floated on off, Bairstow gets a bottom edge on this one.
Loopy ball on middle, defended off the front foot and into the ground.
Plays the square cut this time but straight to the fielder.
Defends this one from within the crease.
Full in length ball outside off. Looks to defend but it hits the inner half of his bat and goes to square leg. They pick up a single.

Slightly short and Stokes looks to pull it across the line off his front foot. He gets a bottom edge and the ball goes past his stumps behind to the right of the keeper. They manage to sneak a single there.
On a good length outside off, left alone by Stokes.
Full length ball on off, played towards covers by Stokes.
Defends this one by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Stokes sweeps this one hard through square leg only for a single.
Floated on middle, played towards mid-wicket this time.
Again a loopy ball on off, played straight back to the bowler.
Loopy ball on middle, played through mid-wicket.
Full length ball on middle, driven towards mid on.
Full length ball on off, defended towards covers this time.
Good length ball on middle, defended from within the crease.
Full on middle, driven through mid on for a couple.
Short ball on middle and Stokes pulls it away. He finds the gap through mid-wicket but only manages to take a single as there is a fielder in the deep.
Defends this one from within the crease.
This one is wide outside off and Stokes leaves it alone.

FOUR! No Ball for overstepping, not a good start at all! Starts the over with a boundary! This was a low full toss and it was asking for the treatment. Stokes smacks it through mid off and gets four runs for the shot.
Theunis de Bruyn comes on to bowl
FOUR! That is fullish and Bairstow goes down to sweep it. He connects well and gets it through gap on square leg. The ball races away to the boundary.
Full length ball on middle. Played off the front foot and into the ground.
Another loopy ball on off, played towards point.
Flighted on off, played off the front foot towards covers.
On the pads this time, worked down the leg side.
Flighted on off, gets on his front foot and defends it into the ground.
Back of a length ball on off, played off the back foot back to the bowler.
On a good length ball but this time towards the pads. Bairstow flicks it past square leg for a single.
Another good length ball, played back to the bowler off the front foot.
Good length ball outside off, pushed towards covers straight to the fielder.
Good length ball just outside off. Too close for the cut but Stokes still goes for it. He misses the ball and it goes straight into the gloves of the keeper.
Full length ball on off, played off the front foot past the bowler to mid off.
Defends this one by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Similar ball, Bairstow pushes it through covers for a single.
Floated on off, Bairstow gets on his front foot and drives it through the covers.
Loopy ball on off, played off the front foot and into the ground.
Width given, Bairstow plays it to point but straight to the fielder.
Loopy ball on middle, defended from within the crease by Bairstow.
Maharaj to continue.
Drinks has been taken.
Stokes gets right behind the line of the delivery to defend this one into the ground.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends this one off the back foot.
Another length ball on off, driven towards mid off by Stokes.

FOUR! Wide outside off and Stokes slashes hard at it. He cuts it past the fielder at point to find the boundary. The ball races away as four more runs are added to the total. 200 runs are on the board!
On the pads, flicked away down the leg side.

Length ball driven straight back to the bowler. Bairstow at the non-strikers end dives back into the crease as Olivier collects the ball. However, he was aiming to throw it back to the batsman instead.
Gets right behind the line of the delivery to defend it.
Loopy ball on middle, played off the front foot and into the ground.
Floated on middle this time, punches off the front foot back to the middle.
Another one floated on off, Bairstow gets on his back foot and punches it into the ground.
Loopy ball on middle, Bairstow defends it into the ground.

NOT OUT! The ball is short and the crowd boos Elgar! Well, well, well. Full and outside off, Bairstow looked to defend. He was hit on the pads and immediately de Kock and Maharaj went up in an appeal. Umpire Dharmasena shook his head, indicating bat. Now, Dean Elgar walked over from first slip, claiming the catch! Umpire Dharmasena now has a discussion with Aleem Dar asking whether the ball carried and then referred it upstairs, with the soft signal being out. The very first replay shows the ball landing short! Oh dear... Elgar better not go to the boundary today. He will get a lot of welcoming reception...

Excitement and drama! There has been an LBW appeal against Bairstow which has been turned down by umpire Dharmasena. Now, the Proteas appeal for a catch and after some discussion, Dharmasena raises his finger! Stokes and Bairstow are bemused and it is being referred upstairs for the catch now...
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
FOUR! Nice shot. Half volley outside off, driven through the covers for a boundary!
Comes forward and pushes it towards mid on.
Full and outside off, pushed back to the bowler.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Full and around off, spinning away, Bairstow lunges and defends.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Landed outside off, left alone.
Outside off, worked through mid-wicket for a single from the crease.
Landed around off, watchfully defended.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended.
Outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
FOUR! Fullish and on the pads, Bairstow clips it to the square leg fence.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full on middle, clipped straight to short mid-wicket.
JONNY BAIRSTOW walks in at number 7, replacing Root.

OUT! He has to go! The review does not save the England skipper! It was a full length ball around off and swinging in late. Root went across for the flick but missed it completely. This looked plumb to the naked eye and the umpire immediately raised his finger. Root walked up to Stokes asking what he felt about the review. Ben thought about it before telling him to go for a second opinion. The replays showed that the ball was going on to hit the leg stump and Root has to walk back to the pavilion. De Kock is the most relieved because of the missed chance earlier in the day. Olivier is pumped up because this is the big fish.
Joe Root has been adjudged lbw! He has a long chat with Stokes and eventually takes the review. It looks very close...
Again, he looks to drive but does not quite time this ball that well. It goes off the toe end of the bat towards the bowler.
Full and outside off, Stokes looks to drive but finds covers.
Root gets to the pitch of the delivery and drives this towards mid off for a single.
Loopy ball on middle, defended solidly by Root.
Change of gloves for Root.
Another full length ball, driven straight past the bowler to his left for a single.
Full and almost a yorker, Stokes hits it hard into the ground.
Another full length ball, defended off the front foot.
Full length ball, driven towards mid on. No runs taken.
Full length ball, driven straight back.
Another wide ball outside the line of the ball. Root leaves it alone.
Wide outside off, Root leaves it alone.
Good length ball on middle, played to mid-wicket.
Slightly short, punched off the back foot for a single.
Full on middle, driven through mid on for a single.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends this one off the back foot.
Shows the full face of the delivery and defends it off the back foot.
Tries to sweep this fullish delivery but misses it completely. He gets struck on the pads and fielders appeal. The umpire says no as it was way across the line there.
Floated on middle and leg, worked down the leg side.
Back of a length ball, defended off the back foot towards mid off. Single taken.
Root gets to his 30th Test fifty. It is his 10th consecutive Test half century.
On the pads, nudged down fine leg for a single.
Back of a length ball, defended off the back foot.
Full length ball, driven straight back by Root to the bowler who parries the ball to mid on. They think of a single but decide against it.
Angling into the pads, Root looks to clip but misses. He gets struck on the pads.
On the pads, worked down the leg side at mid-wicket where Bavuma made a good stop.
Duanne Olvier gets a change of ends.
Stokes defends this one off the front foot and into the ground.

Loud shout for lbw but the umpire stays put. This one was floated on off and Stokes went for sweep. He missed the ball completely and and got struck on the pads. The impact was outside the line of the stumps and hence Stokes is saved.
Fuller in length this time. Root drives it to mid on for a single.
Slightly shorter from Root, defended off the front foot by Root.
Another one outside off, played straight to point.
Outside off, Root plays a square cut but it goes straight to the fielder.
Back of a length ball on off, Stokes rocks onto his back foot and punches it away for a couple. The couple could have been avoided if not for the misfield at mid on.
5000 Test runs for Joe Root! Fifth fastest English batsman to achieve this feat in terms of innings.

There it is! Milestone for Root. Another one. He reaches the 5K mark. It is full on off and he drives it down the ground through mid off. The fielder gives it a good chase and gets to the cherry as it does not have in it to reach the fence. Three runs taken again.
Wide outside off, Root leaves it alone.
On a good length, Stokes stays in his crease and punches it  through mid-wicket. They manage three runs there.
Good length ball, played straight back to the bowler.
Stokes chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Flighted on middle again, defended off the front foot and into the ground.
Floated on middle, driven through mid on.
Fullish in length, Root defends it off his front foot.

Edged but safe! That was flighted on off and Stokes looked to defend. he ball took the edge and flew past the outstretched arms of the fielder at slip. Three runs taken as the ball trickles towards third man.
Loopy ball outside off, played to point for a single.
Bowls this one a fraction short and Stokes cuts through the square on the off side. Three runs taken.
Maharaj is back on. Just the one over for Olivier after the break.

EDGED, BUT NOT TAKEN! FOUR! For once, de Kock does not dive. Big moment in the game. Poor, poor Morkel. He cannot believe it. He has bowled his heart out. He was trying to work Root over and bowled a pearler. He bowled this on a length, just outside off and forced Root to defend. Then he got the ball to move away and take the outside edge. It is a simple regulation catch for Quinton de Kock but he does not budge. Neither does Amla at first slip, who is hoping that de Kock will move to his right. In the end, the ball goes right between the two to the third man fence. Gosh. Tea pots must be boiling in Morkel's mind right now. He does not say a word. Nothing to the batsman in frustration or to the keeper. Just takes his cap and walks off, like a well-behaved boy from high school. Nice lad. South Africa will hope Root will be as nice and gives another chance. SOON.
Short and wide outside off, curving away after pitching, Joe flashes hard but misses out.
Outside off, quietly left alone.
Fullish and around off, coming in, pushed back to the bowler.
Oooh... nearly! Full and outside off, Root looks to drive, a bit loosely too, no feet movement and almost pays the price by nearly nicking it. The ball moves away late and beats the outside edge.
Landed outside off, Root pushes it towards point.
The batsman defends it from within the crease. 13 from the over!
Around middle and off, very tight, better from Olivier and Ben defends.

FOUR! The runs are leaking. It has been a poor start from Olivier after Tea. He overcompensates for the previous ball by bowling this too full and Stokes promptly flicks it through mid-wicket for a boundary. Third of the over.
FOUR! Bad ball, short and  around middle, Stokes swivels and pulls it to the fine leg fence.
Around middle and leg, Joe tucks it through square leg, wants two, takes the single but then changes his mind.

FOUR! LOVELY! Loosener from Olivier, bowls a half volley wide outside off, Root leans and drives it through the covers for a boundary! 3000 TEST RUNS AT HOME for the skipper. Third youngest after his predecessor and the great Sachin Tendulkar to achieve this feat.
DUANNE OLIVIER to bowl from the other end. Maharaj bowled 16 overs on the bounce before Tea. Wasn't given a rest, he is given now.
A similar line, not as full as the previous one, Stokes drives it in a better manner but cannot beat mid off.
A tempter, full and just outside off, BS looks for the drive but mistimes it towards mid off.
The length is dragged even shorter and this time Ben pushes it towards mid off.

Shane Warne on air feels that it has been a great contest between bat and ball so far. He also reckons that the pitch will quicken up as the game progresses, so batting will actually be easier on Days 2 and 3.
The line is around off, but the length is slightly short of full, Stokes comes forward and pushes it towards mid on.
Landed outside off, allowed to go through.
Short and outside off, cut past Temba Bavuma at gully for a single.
The players are back in the middle. It will be MORNE MORKEL vs JOE ROOT first up...
... DAY 1, SESSION 3 ...

Overall, South Africa will be very pleased with how they have bowled so far. The quicks have fairly tight, not giving anything away and the run rate is still under 3 an over. They will aim to get at least 3 more wickets before close, given the purchase present on this pitch. Join us back at 1600 local (1500 GMT) for the final session. The over-rate has been decent, which means, only 33 overs left to be bowled.

Joe Root has Ben Stokes with him in the middle now and will hope that they can stitch a partnership. England are not exactly in a mire but they are not out of the woods either. As the great Geoffrey Boycott says - Add two wickets to the total and then view the game. The hosts have a deep batting line-up and will back themselves to avert a collapse. Root today, has been very cautious, unlike his flashy innings earlier in this series.

Not a bad session at all, if you are a South African fan. Cook, Westley and Malan have been sent back to the hut and not a single half century has been scored. The runs continue to come in trifles, with only 80 runs coming in 28 overs in this session.
Another one wide outside off, Root plays it to point for a single. THAT IS TEA ON DAY 1!
Outside off, played towards the point region.
Outside off, Stokes goes for it but finds the edge. The ball goes through the slip region for a single. Luckily for him it was well wide of the slip fielder.
Outside off, played towards point this time.
Plays this one off the front foot and into the ground.
Fraction short and Root punches it off his back foot to the off side for a single.
Ben Stokes is the new man in.

OUT! The change of angle does the trick for Morkel. It was a good length ball outside off and Malan went for the drive. He did not time it well enough and the ball found the nick. Du Plessis at second slip took a good sharp catch to dismiss Malan. South Africa will be delighted to get their man right before Tea.
Wide outside off, Malan leaves it alone.
Once again wide outside off, Root plays a square cut for a single.
Bye. Second extra of the day and it's a bye. This was wide outside off and Malan left it alone. The ball goes through the slips and the batsmen sneak in a single.
Edges this one wide outside off ball as he goes for the ball. However it lands just in front of the fielder at gully. Malan needs to be careful.
Morkel goes from around to over the wicket.
Good length ball on off, defended solidly by Malan.
Another front foot defense by Root.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Air given to this one on off, played off the front foot and into the ground.
50-run partnership between Malan and Root.
Floated on middle and off, driven towards mid off for a single. These two consolidated the innings so far.
Loopy ball on off, played off the front foot and into the ground.
Floated on middle, played straight back to the bowler.
Full length ball on off, driven through the covers for a single.
Once again outside off, played to the point region. No run taken this time.
Slightly outside off, Root cuts it towards point for a single.
Back of a length, defended off the back foot by Root.
Another one on the pads, Malan flicks it to the leg side for a single this time.

FOUR! Good length going down the leg side and all Malan needed was to get something on it. He flicks and helps the ball to fine leg for the boundary. De Kock puts in a despairing dive but gets nowhere near the ball.
Defends this one by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Root goes for the sweep but it goes straight to the fielder at square leg.
Slightly outside off, Root looks to cut but gets a bottom edge that goes to the slip fielder.
Loopy ball on middle, played straight back to the bowler.
Floated on off, driven through the covers.
Loopy ball on the pads, flicked to the leg side for a single.
Wide outside off, Root shoulders arms at it.
Full length ball on middle, Root plays across the line to the mid-wicket region for a couple. Bavuma does well to chase it down and stop the boundary.
FOUR! Slightly outside off, on a good length. Root uses the width given to cut the ball past backward point for the boundary. Good shot by Joe Root.
Once again bowls a full length ball, played straight back to the bowler.
Full and straight on off, another solid forward defense by the English skipper.
Slightly full outside on off. Root plays a forward defense to the off side.
Comes down the track and plays this one back to the bowler.
Drives this straight one back to the bowler.
Loopy ball on middle. flicked to mid wicket for a single.
Forward defense this time back to the bowler.
On the pads, defended into the ground back to the bowler.
Loopy ball in middle, defended towards short extra cover.
Landed outside off, fairly wide to be playing at, Dawid lets it through.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
Around off, watchfully defended from the crease.
Falls over a bit, does Root but manages to flick it fine for a run.
On middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket for a single.
Landed outside off, left alone.
MORNE MORKEL is back into the attack.
ALMOST! Maharaj nearly gets his man. Full on middle, Root chips this uppishly but luckily for him, it does not carry to short mid-wicket.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman.
On middle and leg, pushed towards mid on.
Full and outside off, watchfully driven towards cover.
Outside off, watchfully defended.
Full and outside off, Root defends it watchfully.
That ball has taken the inside edge onto the pads.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
Gets the flick shot this time, past square leg for a single.
The arm ball outside off, let through.
Back of a length outside off, forced through the off side for a couple.

NOT OUT. Height was the issue. It did look that way on the first look, to be fair. But guess the review was taken because the umpire indicated the ball to be going down the leg side. It was on a good length, angled in from outside off, beating Root on his defense. Root was a bit further ahead of his crease, so height would have always come into play. However, when Rabada appealed, umpire Aleem Dar signalled it going down the leg side and on seeing that, Faf went for the review. Hawk Eye showed that to be clipping the top of the stumps. So close.
Okay... so South Africa have taken a review here. It has come after a lot of deliberation. Let's see... this could be a big wicket if they get it.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.
This time he drives it towards mid off again but Maharaj stops it.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off.
Similar ball, watchfully blocked out.
Landed around off, watchfully defended.
Fullish on middle, pushed towards mid on.
Interesting. Having seen Root play a shot very fine in his previous over Maharaj has asked for a leg gully.
Half volley outside off, Malan looks to drive but misses.
Rabada holds the length back a touch now, angles it across the southpaw and respecting Kagiso's respect, DM lets it go.

FOUR! HANDSOME! Almost similar to the previous ball but this time Malan does not let it go. The ball is not exactly a half volley, perhaps a touch shorter than that, Malan leans into it and drives it beautifully through the covers.
Wider outside off, left alone.
Goes back in his crease this time and blocks.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
FOUR! Gets that very fine, does the skipper. This is down the leg side and Root gets down and sweeps it very fine. Morne Morkel starts to give it a chase from fine leg but the ball wins the race.
Flighted outside off, Dawid comes down the track and defends.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman.
Slips this on the pads, Malan tucks it through fine leg. Temba Bavuma gives it a good chase from backward square leg, slides and slips, conceding the second.
Full and outside off, Malan watches that out comfortably.
Landed outside off, left alone.
Around off, clipped straight to short mid-wicket.

EDGED, FOUR! The break almost does the batsman in! Root gets away with that one. Full and wide outside off, Root is sucked into the drive and goes hard after it. Gets a thick outside edge which flies past second slip to the third man fence.

Okay... Good news coming up. The gentleman who had fainted in the crowd has regained consciousness and seems fairly okay. The resumption should not take long now. The ambulance is taking the gentleman to the hospital, perhaps.

We are still not quite ready to resume. There is some issue regarding the seating arrangement of the crowd near the sightscreen. It is regarding some serious medical issue to someone in the crowd. Good sportsmanship shown by the players, as they feel it is disrespectful to continue when someone is getting medical attention. It is right behind the bowler's arm.

There seems to be some issue within the crowd. Does not look like it is going to be sorted quickly and the umpires call for a Drinks Break. Common sense prevails. Good period of play for the Proteas. Since the Lunch break, they have managed the wickets of Cook and Westley. They will now hope to get rid of Root as quickly as possible and burst through that middle order. Easily said than done though.
Another inside edge this time. Aloud appeal has been turned down by the umpire. Once again Root mistimes his shot but is saved by the inside edge off the good length ball.
On the pads, Root flicked away for a couple.

Nasser Hussain provides an interesting observation regarding Malan's footwork. Ever since Rabada knocked his stumps the previous time he was dismissed by the youngster, Malan has stopped twitching with his back foot. He has looked to be more compact and more composed. In that Test, he kept falling over to fullish deliveries. Even today, when he arrived a crease, Rabada attempted a similar delivery, it was full and Dawid did miss the flick but he did not fall over as much as he did the other day.
Loud appeal for an lbw but the umpire is not interested. It was a good length ball on middle and Root looked to defend. The ball took an inside edge before hitting the pads which is what saved him.
Outside off, played to the point region by Root.
Wide outside off, Root plays a square cut and picks up three runs.
Root gets right behind the line of the delivery to defends this one.
Gets to the picth of the ball and plays this one for a single.
On the pads, Root looks to play at it but gets an edge. He manages to pick up a single.
FOUR! That's a very good shot by Root. It was a loopy ball on off and Root got to the pitch of the delivery to drive it through covers for the boundary.
Outside off and slightly full, pushed to the cover region for a single.
Outside off, Root misses the line of the delivery this time.
Bouncer! Root gets under it to duck the delivery.

Back of a length this time, Root looks to defend but gets a bottom edge and falls to the leg side. Cook did not take any chance and made sure he was ready to block it if the ball would go on to hot the stumps.

Big shout for lbw but the umpire is not interested. It was a good length ball on middle and Root failed to get his bat on ball. Replays showed that the ball was anyways going on to miss the top of the stumps. Good decision by the umpire there.
Gets right behind the line of the delivery to defend this one.
Wide outside off, Root plays a square cut this time.
Gets to the pitch of the delivery and defends this one.
Another front foot defensive shot by Malan there.
Malan gets right behind the line of the delivery and defends this one solidly.
Once again a fractionally shorter ball on middle, played off the front foot and into the ground.
On a length on middle, played towards to mid-wicket.
Slightly on the shorter side, defended off the back foot this time by Malan.
On the pads, Malan looks to play but misses it completely. The ball strikes him on the pads but the umpire is not interested.
Wide outside off, Malan shoulders his arms at it.
Outside off, Malan fails to put bat on ball.
Dawid Malan is the new man in.

OUT! Westley departs! Rabada has his man. But this has to be attributed to the keeper de Kock. Rabada kept this on a length, just outside off and got it to straighten a touch. Westley felt for it and got a thick outside edge. The ball further kept moving away but de Kock dived to his right and took a stunner. Just one of those de Kock catches. Brilliant. Absolutely brilliant. The keeper had to go for the catch as it would not have carried to Hashim Amla at first slip.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Root shows the full face of the bat to defend this into the ground.
Gets right behind the line of the delivery to defend this straight one.
Floated on middle, defended from within the crease by Root.
Full length ball on middle, driven through mid off this time.
Loopy ball on middle, defended off the front foot.
On the pads, Root plays it to square leg.
Bouncer! Westley ducks under it.
Westley shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Another one outside off, left alone.
Westley shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Outside off, Westley leaves it alone.
Loopy ball on middle, Westley defends it off his back foot.
Good length ball on middle, defended from within the crease by Root.
Root has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Good length ball on middle, defended solidly by Root.
Joe Root walks in the middle now.

OUT! Cook has been done in by the spinner on 46! Just short of a half-century and this will hurt the opener. He did all the hard work of settling in and then gets done in by the straighter one. Cook got on his front foot and looked to push it through covers but the ball took a faint outside edge which went into the gloves of the keeper. Cook has been dismissed by a spinner for the first time in this series. South Africa will be delighted with this start!
Full length ball on middle, driven through mid on for a single.
On the pads, flicked away by Westley.
Good length ball on middle, played to mid-wicket this time.
Straight and on middle, played through mid-wicket by Westley. The ball looks to be going for a boundary but it's stopped. Three runs taken.
Way wide outside off this time, left alone by Westley.
Good length ball outside off, Westley leaves it alone.
Good length ball wide outside off. Cook cuts it past point and takes three runs. Bavuma does really well to chase it down and stop the boundary.
Good length ball on middle, defended solidly by Cook.
Rababa comes back on to bowl.
Westley has defended the loopy ball on middle by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Floated on middle and off, pushed to covers this time.
Straight on middle, driven towards mid on by Westley.
Floated on middle and leg, smacked to mid-wicket.
Another loopy ball on middle, Westley gets on his front foot and defends it well.
Loopy ball but it's full on middle, defended easily by Westley.
Length ball on off, Cook plays a forward defense straight down the ground.
Back of a length this time, defends it from within the crease towards gully.
Outside off, Cook plays a good looking square drive but it is a good stop by Bavuma at point.
Full length ball on off, defended off the front foot by Cook.
On middle, Cook plays this one through mid-wicket for a couple.
Full length ball on middle, driven straight back down the ground.
FOUR! Brilliant shot this time by Westley. Floated on middle, Westley drives it through mid on for a boundary. Westley has started to find the touch now.
Loopy ball on off, driven through covers by Westley.
Westley defends this by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Flighted on off, pushed to the cover region.
Floated on middle, punched off the back foot this time.
Loopy ball on off, Westley looks to defend it but finds an outside edge. The ball goes past slips and they manage a couple.

FOUR! Back of a length ball and Cook was ready for it. He got into the position to pull it over square leg and found the boundary. De Bruyn put in a dive but it was in vain as the ball went past the ropes.
Good length ball on middle, defended back to the bowler.
Another full length ball on off. Cook drives it through the off side for a couple wide of mid off.
Full length ball on middle, defended off the back foot this time. Cook looks to have settled himself in the middle now.

FOUR! Cook finds the gap to perfection square on the off side. It was full length ball outside off, Cook just opened the face of his bat to find the boundary. Superb timing by the former England skipper.
Good length ball on off, played off the front foot towards the off side. Solid defense by Cook.
Flighted on off, played off the front foot towards the off side.
Floated on middle and off, played straight back to the bowler.
Loopy ball on middle, played to mid-wicket by Westley.
Fuller this time, played off the front foot and into the ground.
Back of length this time, defended off the back foot this time.
Loopy ball outside off, Cook moves to his front foot but watches it go into the keepers gloves.
Maharaj to bowl from the other end.
Good length ball on off, defended into the ground on the off side. Maiden over by Olivier.
Fuller length ball on middle, driven to mid on.
Cook stays adamant with the balls outside off. Leaves this one alone as well.
On a good length outside off, left alone by Cook.
Problems in the sightscreen for Cook but it gets sorted out.
Another good length ball on middle, defended from within the crease.
Good length ball on off, defended towards covers by Cook.

The players are back in the middle as we get ready for the second session. Will South Africa make more inroads or can England settle in and go on to make a good score? Let's find out. Olivier to start the proceedings with Cook on strike.
...Day 1, Session 2...

Cook has been fighting hard and looks settled in the middle now with Westley on the other end. The newcomer looked tentative at the start but he slowly played himself in and even played some good looking shots. It's turning into a good battle between the batsmen and bowlers with South Africa looking more dangerous. The scoring rate is very slow but England won't mind that. Towards the end, dark clouds seemed to be coming in but if they stay away, batting will surely get easier. The second session promises to be as interesting as this so do join us for that.

Superb first session of cricket! South Africa, rocked by the ruling out of Morris and Philander have surprisingly started off on a strong footing. They caused early problems for the openers and the overcast conditions were surely helping them. Jennings was having a tough time in the middle and in the end, Olivier got his man with a regulation nick.
On middle, played to mid-wicket by Westley. THAT'S LUNCH ON DAY 1!
Defends this one by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Loopy ball on middle, defended solidly by Westley.
Loopy ball on middle, played off the front foot and into the ground.
Loopy ball on middle, defended off the front foot by Westley.

That's a jaffa! Maharaj comes from around the wicket and bowls this one on the off stump. The ball turns slightly away from the bat of Westley who looked to play a forward defensive shot. It goes past his outside edge and into the gloves of the keeper. A spinners delight this!
Straight and on the pads, Cook stays in his crease and defends it back to the bowler.
On a length, defended off the back foot to the off side.
Good length ball on middle, defended from within the crease.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends it off his back foot.
Good length ball on middle, defends it from within the crease.
Down the leg side this time, Cook leaves it alone.
Back of a length, punched off the back foot towards covers.
On the pads, Cook works it down the leg side for an easy single.
Flighted ball on off, played off the front foot and into the ground.
Wide outside off, Cook rocks back and plays a square cut towards point. Good stop by the fielder there.
Floated on off, Cook plays it off his front foot towards covers.
Loopy ball on middle, Cook works it to the leg side.
Maharaj comes back on to bowl.
This time Westley lets the ball outside off go.
Outside off, this time Westley goes for it and makes a mistake. He goes with soft hands and edges it towards gully. The ball falls short there.
Another one outside off, Westley leaves it alone once again.
Wide outside off once again, this time Westley sensibly leaves it alone.

FOUR! Short and wide outside off and Westley slashes his bat at it. He is lucky that he went hard as the ball flew over the first slip fielder for a boundary. Streaky runs but South Africa won't mind this. The bowlers are surely creating doubts in the batsman's mind.
On the pads, flicked away for a single down the leg side.
Change of ends for Olivier.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends this off the back foot.
FOUR! Good length ball by de Bruyn and Westley times it well. He gets on his back foot and punches it past covers for a boundary. That was a sweet shot by Westley there.
On the pads, worked away down the leg side for a single.
Struck on the pads this time but safe. This one was going down leg hence Cook got away with it.
Low full toss this time, driven through mid off.
Full length ball on middle, driven through mid on.
Amla has now gone off the field possibly for a break.
This time he defends this good length ball off the back foot.
Outside edge but does not carry. That was a good length ball on off and Westley looked to defend it. The ball takes a faint edge but falls short of the fielder at third slip.
Outside off this time, Westley lets it go.
Full length ball on middle and off. Driven through mid-on by Westley.
FOUR! Fuller length ball and it has been dispatched nicley by Westley. He moves slightly across to make space for flick through mid-wicket. The ball races away as two fielders try to chase it down.
Good length ball on off, defended solidly into the ground by Westley.
Good news for South Africa, Maharaj is back on the field.
Lands this outside off, let through.
Full and wide outside off, driven through the covers for a single.
Outside off, left alone.
Goes further down the leg side, flicked away for a single.
Oohh.... looks to flick but gets a leading edge which dies down on the pitch.
Slips this down the leg side, Cook misses his flick.
Interesting. THEUNIS DE BRUYN has been given the ball. Bowls medium pace. Nasser Hussain says that these are the sort of bowlers who irritate Cook in domestic cricket.
Outside off, left alone.
This is around off, Westley feels for it but misses.
Around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They pick up a single.
Fullish outside off, driven through the covers for a couple.
Full and around off, Cook looks to defend but the ball comes in, takes the inside edge and goes to the leg side.
Maharaj is off the field. Looks like the injury is serious. South Africa will be ruing their luck as injuries have been haunting them throughout this series.
Straighter one this time, driven straight to mid off.
On the pads this time, flicked away past fine leg for a single.
Loopy ball on middle, defended off the front foot and into the ground.
Flighted on middle, Cook looks to defend but gets an inside edge. Luckily for him it does not carry to short leg.
On the pads, worked down the leg side.
Loopy ball on middle, driven to mid on.
Looks like Maharaj is having some problems. The physio has come but Maharaj looks good to go after the consultation.
Good length ball on off, Westley lets it go.

Nice observation from Shaun Pollock on air. He keenly sees the change in seam position from Duanne Olivier. In the second Test that he played, his seam position was more towards second slip and hence, he could not control it. Today, he landed the seam in a proper position and beat the outside edge of Westley and also got the wicket of Jennings. Brilliant point.
Outside off this time, Westley leaves it alone.
Gets right behind the line of the delivery this time and defends it solidly.
FOUR! Fuller length delivery by Morkel and it has been given the treatment. Westley drives it solidly past mid on for a boundary. Welcome runs for the new man in as he slowly settling in.
Another one outside off, Westley chooses to leave it alone.
Outside off this time, Westley looks to defend but misses it.
Plays this one off the front foot and into the ground.
Once again bowls on a same length. Cook defends it solidly.
Flighted on off, played into the ground back to the bowler.
Defended solidly off the front foot this time.
Another similar ball, Cook drives it to mid on this time.
Loopy ball on off, pushed towards mid off.
Keshav Maharaj comes on to bowl some spin.
Westley was beaten and missed the line of the delivery.
Bouncer! Westley ducks in time to let that one go over him.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman.
Outside off, left alone by Westley.
Good length ball on middle, defended off the front foot by Westley.
Going towards leg, Westley works it down the leg side this time for a single.
Beaten this time. It was going wide outside off but Westley missed the forward defense
Another one wide outside off, Westley shoulders his arms at it.
Outside off this time, Westley once again leaves it alone.
Wide outside off this time, left alone by Westley.
Bouncer! Westley picks this one early and leaves it alone.
Outside off this time, pushed towards covers, straight to the fielder.
Good length ball on middle, defended off the back foot.
Struck on the pads but going down the leg side. Cook has gotten his eye in but is till missing the ball time and again.
Full length  ball this time, driven straight down the ground.
Cook has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Defends this one by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Morkel begins the first over after drinks.

Drinks break has been taken. South Africa have made a really good start as they have been tormenting the English batsmen with the balls aimed at the pads. The overcast conditions early on really helped the bowlers but the weather has improved lately.
Good length ball on off, Westley shoulders his arms at it.
On the pads, Cook flicks it away for a single.
Outside off this time, Cook leaves it alone.

FOUR! Majestic shot from Cook this time. It was a full length ball on off and all Cook did was time it. He drove it past the bowler as the ball raced towards the boundary ropes at long off. Maharaj puts in a desperate dive but fails to stop it.
Left alone by Cook this time as the ball goes outside off.
Outside off, Cook fails to put bat on ball.
Another escape for Westley. He looks to defend the ball on off but only bottom edges it past his stumps.

Close! Westley is really having a torrid time so far. The ball jagged in from off onto his back pad as he looked to defend. It flew towards Amla at first slip who did not pouch it. Luckily for Westley there was no inside edge there.
Once again the ball outside off has been left alone.
Outside off, Westley shoulders his arms at it.
Struck on the pads this time. It was a good length ball but was going on to miss the stumps. Westley needs to be more careful.
Another one outside off by Rabada who has been following this line. Westley has nothing to do with it.
On the pads this time, flicked away for a single at mid-wicket.
Bouncer! Westley ducks under it and lets it go.
Westley is following the footsteps of the batsman he replaces. Another one outside off and he misses the defense as he gets outfoxed by away movement of the ball.
Another one outside off, Westley fails to put bat on ball.
Wide outside off, left alone by the new batsman in.
Tom Westley is the new man in.

Edged and gone! Another failure for Jennings who has been put out of his misery. It was a good length ball from Olivier and Jennings pushed at it. The ball found the outside edge of the bat and flew straight into the gloves of de Kock. It was a regulation catch for the keeper and he made no mistake. South Africa have their first wicket and will be hoping to carry on with their good start.

Another full length ball on off. Jennings goes for the drive but it takes the edge of the bat and flies towards backward point. It was in the air but was finding the gap. Bavuma did well to save a boundary there. Single taken.
Full length this time, defended off the front foot.
On the pads, flicked away for a single.
Length ball on off, pushed to covers.
Shows the full face of the bat to defend this one off the back foot.
FOUR! Bouncer down the leg side by Rabada. Cook loves the short balls and he goes for it. He misses it but the ball brushes his gloves and goes past the diving keeper for a boundary.
Outside off, driven straight past the bowler for a couple.
Outside off, Jennings shoulders his arms at it.
Shows the full face of the bat and defends this one off the back foot.
On a good length, defended solidly off the back foot.
FOUR! Driven beautifully through covers! That was a full length ball on off and Jennings played it with the full face of the bat.

Struck on the pads this time but. It was a good length ball outside off which Jennings went to defend. He gets struck on his back pads and the appeal came in. The umpire however dismisses the shout as it was going on to miss the stumps.

It has grown considerably bright at the moment when it looked like the weather would play spoilsport. David Lloyd opines that the predicted bad weather will not be a problem as of now as the dark clouds have gone by.
Stays back in his crease and blocks.
Oohhh..... this is straighter, Alastair looks to flick, is late but manages to flick it through backward square leg for a couple.
This is around off, defended back to the bowler.
Outside off now, left alone.
Cannot control the swing and movement on this one, Rabada slips this down the leg side and Alastair looks to flick but misses.
Excellent bowling. This is pitched outside leg, Cook feels for it but then the ball shapes away and beats the outside edge.
Keeps this on a length outside off, Keaton feels for it but then the ball moves away and beats him.
Outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Do not bowl there. However bad shape the batsman may be in. Jennings latches on to it and crashes it in front of point for a boundary.
Outside off, left alone this time.
Good length ball and Jennings is really flirting with danger. He looks to defend it but misses it completely. The ball just misses the outside edge.
Good length ball on off, Jennings looks to play at it but misses.
Olivier come on to bowl. He replaces Morkel.
Another one wide outside off, played to point this time.

FOUR! Brilliantly timed by Cook. Width was on the offer and Cook obliged with a hard slash past point. The ball raced away to the boundary ropes in no time. It was slightly in the air but found the gap to perfection. England will need more of this.
Length ball on off this time, Cook drives it straight to covers.
Shows the full face of the bat to defend this one off his back foot.
Good length ball on off, defended solidly this time. The ball goes to straight to the fielder at point.

Outside edge lands but does not carry. That was a length ball outside off. Cook looked to defend but the timing was off. The ball took a thick edge and flew towards third slip but landed just in front of him.
Struck on the pads this time. A good length ball coming into the batsman. Jennings went for the flick, missed it and the ball struck him high on the pads.
Play and miss this time. Jennings does not look confident at all. This was a good length ball outside off and Jennings went for the drive.
Defends this one by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Outside off this time, Jennings leaves it alone.
On the pads, worked down the leg side for a single.

FOUR! Class from Cook! Full length ball on off, Cook drives it beautifully past mid off and the ball races away. This was a really well timed shot from the veteran. This should go on to give him some confidence.
Bouncer! Jennings ducks in time to let that one go over him. Maiden over for Rabada.
Jennings shoulders arms to let that one through.
Down the leg side this time, Jennings leaves it alone.
Another back of a length ball defended off the back foot.
Solid defense from within the crease. Good length ball once again, good discipline shown by the bowlers.
Jennings shows the full face of the bat and defends this good length ball off the back foot.
Inside edge this time. Length ball on off and Cook looked for the drive. The ball goes on to thud against the pads.
Struck high on the pads once again. The height of Morkel is playing against him at the moment as his balls are going on to miss the top of the stumps.
Defended solidly off his back foot this time. This looked better from the batsman.
Outside off this time. Cook leaves it all alone.
On the pads once again but hit him high this time. Cook looked to play at it but missed it.
Length ball on off, Cook pushes it covers off his front foot and picks up a couple.
Outside off, left alone. Jennings will not mind such balls for sure. They are safer than the ones coming on to his pads.
Once again struck on the pads. This was also pitching outside leg. Jennings needs to get his bat on the ball or his time will be up soon.

Struck on the pads and a loud shout has been turned down. This was a good length ball pitching outside leg and missing leg as well. Nevertheless the bowlers are causing some problems early on. Jennings looked to defend but missed it.
Length ball, Jennings defends it solidly off his front foot.
Outside off, Jennings goes for it but misses.
On the pads, Jennings works it down the leg side and picks up a couple of runs.
Short leg has come in. Good point from Michael Holding on air - Why not start with a bat-pad in the first place? Especially if the plan is to bowl short.

Another shout for lbw which the umpire shows no interest. Same as the previous shout, this was going down leg. Cook does not look too comfortable in the middle at all. The overcast conditions are not helping him.
On middle and leg, Cook plays it to mid-wicket.
Big shout for lbw but the umpire dismisses it. That was a good length ball jutting in. Cook looks to defend but misses. The height factor saves him this time.
Finds the edge of the bat but falls safely this time. Morkel is really causing some problems in the middle.
Good length ball outside off this time. Cook wants nothing to do with it. Leaves it alone.
Cook shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Defends this length ball off his front foot and into the ground.
On off, Jennings pushes it to covers.

Dropped! A good length ball on middle. Jennings looks to defend it but gets an inside edge. The ball goes on to hit his pads and flies in the air. Rabada tries his best and puts in a dive but fails to keep the ball in his clutches. This was difficult but a very good attempt. South Africa will hope it's not too costly for them.

FOUR! First runs of the day and it comes in the form of a boundary. This was on a good length down the leg side. Jennings flicks it off his pads and gets a four behind square on the leg side. This should give him some confidence.
On the stumps this time, Jennings does well to get his bat on it.
Starts with a good length ball outside off. Jennings misses his attempted drive.
Rabada will bowl from the other end.
Cook looks jittery in the middle. Another play and miss outside the line of the off stump.
Good length ball outside off, Cook looks to defend but misses. This was very close to the bat.
On a good length but going down leg. Cook looks to flick but misses. The ball brushes his pads and goes into the gloves of the diving keeper.
That's a beauty by Morkel! Jags this one back at Cook who decides to leave it. In the end, it is well left. Just misses the off stump there.
Another one outside the line of the off stump. Left alone by Cook.
Starts off with a good length ball outside off. Cook leaves it alone as he judges the bounce of the pitch.
The openers are walking out to the middle. Morne Morkel is marking his run up, he will be bowling from the Statham End. Here we go!

TEAM NEWS - England have fielded an unchanged side from the last Test. South Africa on the other hand have been forced to make some drastic changes. Duanne Olivier and Theunis de Bruyn will be replacing Vernon Philander and Chris Morris.
ENGLAND HAVE WON THE TOSS AND ELECTED TO BAT FIRST!
The big news is that both Vernon Philander and Chris Morris have been ruled out of this all-important game for the Proteas. It will be interesting to see how they compensate for the duo.

Hello and welcome to the fourth and final Test of the Basil D'Oliveira Trophy. England have ensured that they cannot lose this series courtesy of their two wins prior to this while South Africa will be playing for a draw. If South Africa pull it off, they will extend their unbeaten run in England since 1998. They have already shown their character after bouncing back strongly in the second match.
